evidence: Marley Marl produced Craig G's 1986 debut single 'Droppin' Science' and the 1988 Juice Crew posse cut 'The Symphony', on which Craig G is one of four featured MCs, as recorded in standard hip-hop histories and reissue liner notes.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Droppin' Science' is a teenager showing off raw speed over a fairly plain Marl beat. Two years later on 'The Symphony', the same fast delivery is deployed with far more control, one verse among four over a single looped horn stab, and it's the verse most often picked out of the four.

explanation: Marley Marl produced Craig G's first record, 'Droppin' Science', in 1986, and put him on 'The Symphony' (1988) alongside Kool G Rap, Big Daddy Kane and Masta Ace, where Craig G's verse is the one most often singled out. It is a straightforward production credit, and a useful contrast with the crew's bigger names: Marl's beat is the constant across both records, and what changes is entirely Craig G's own growth as a rapper.
